pairs.why: A's saddle sits over the rail with one fender and stirrup hanging from it; B's stirrup hangs off the cinch strap on a stray bar that runs behind the rail.
B's camp armchair has armrests fixed to the posts and an X-frame that clearly carries the seat; A's backrest posts stop at the seat and don't clearly join the crossed legs.
Like the real chair, A has a folding X-frame with floor runners and back posts that run down into the frame; B's armrest posts and crossed legs don't clearly meet the seat rail.
B hangs both stirrups side by side under the centre strap with no fenders, when they belong on opposite sides; A's single fender and stirrup hang correctly.
A has labelled number and operator keys like the real card, while B's grid of blank keys couldn't be used as a calculator.
Both saucers have a dome seated on a rimmed disc with lights around the edge, and each is drawn from one consistent camera, so neither is clearly built wrong.
A hangs flat on the wall like the real card; B stands upright on the floor on its round rim with no stand or feet, so it would roll over.
B's yoke clamps to the truss and both arms bolt to the sides of the can; in A the left arm of the yoke ends in mid-air without reaching the can.
